question: Who is referred to as the 'Father of the Indian Renaissance' due to their contribution in social reform, literary works and unwavering patriotism?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Ram Mohan Roy.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy is called the 'Father of the Indian Renaissance' for his immense contribution to social, religious, and educational reforms in India during the 19th century.**
 
• **He played a pivotal role in the abolition of the inhuman practice of Sati in 1829, with the help of Lord William Bentinck.**
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a strong advocate for women's rights, including widow remarriage and women's education.**
 
• He founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828, which aimed to reform and modernize the social and religious practices of Hinduism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dayanand Saraswati:** He was the founder of the Arya Samaj, a Hindu reform movement. He advocated for the return to the Vedas and opposed idol worship, caste discrimination, and child marriage. His slogan "Back to the Vedas" aimed at reviving the ancient Indian culture and knowledge.
 
• **Swami Vivekananda:** A disciple of Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa, Swami Vivekananda played a crucial role in introducing Indian philosophies like Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world. He is famous for his speech at the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago in 1893, where he addressed the audience as "Sisters and Brothers of America."
 
• **Atmaram Pandurang:** He was a social reformer and one of the founders of the Prarthana Samaj, a reformist movement in Maharashtra. The Prarthana Samaj aimed to remove caste discrimination and promote widow remarriage, women's education, and other social reforms.
